entries.note: The sender printed the label and has not handed the shipment over; the reply's own text for the scan is this wording.
Wording from the tracker's English page text. Its place names the office or logistics centre, the recipient's pickup office included.
The adapter appends the line's route, which the reply names.
Accepted when no office or line scan comes before it, as a courier collecting from the sender, else out for delivery. The reply names the courier, which the adapter drops.
The adapter appends the reason in brackets and takes the office the courier brought the parcel back to as its place.
The tracker shows no name with it; the adapter reads none.
An order changing the shipment's terms, such as its delivery office. The adapter appends the order's subject and drops its number. Left without a stage: the parcel does not move.
A label of the tracker's page text.
A label of the tracker's page text; the Bulgarian label reads "връщане на пратката", the shipment's return.
A label of the tracker's page text.
A label of the tracker's page text, without a milestone.
The reply flags scans of the return receipt, which Econt's API documentation describes; the adapter files them under this code without a stage, whatever their kind.
A shipment's summary status; its Latin form reads "Delivered".
Summary status, Latin form "At office". Ready for pickup when the reply names the office storing the parcel; otherwise the newest scan decides.
Summary status, Latin form "Awaiting delivery to Econt".
A summary status Econt's API documentation lists.
Read like "В офис": ready for pickup only when the reply names the office storing the parcel.
With a courier, collecting or delivering: the newest scan decides.
On its way back to the sender, not yet returned.
